rows.proposed_test: Review exact reference reactions, domains and catalytic residues; assay candidate proteins using every required input in the parent hypothesis, with authentic product standards, a characterized reference and no-enzyme controls. Establish direction and tissue compatibility before claiming a Cannabis pathway.

document.claim_boundary: EC/name-only discovery with no automatic exact-reaction assignment. Both reviewed and unreviewed records retained with source annotations. Cofactor specificity, reference assay identity, Cannabis activity, reaction direction and in-vivo flux are unverified. Any passing homology is an experimental lead only, ineligible for model integration. Atom tracing deferred.

document.review_decision: Keep the lead ineligible. The selected match overlaps an annotated isopropylmalate-dehydrogenase-like domain in both sequences; the broad reference name is not evidence of ureidoglycolate catalysis by that region.

texts.value: Catalyzes the oxidation of 3-carboxy-2-hydroxy-4-methylpentanoate (3-isopropylmalate) to 3-carboxy-4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate. The product decarboxylates to 4-methyl-2 oxopentanoate
Binds 1 Mg(2+) or Mn(2+) ion per subunit.
Amino-acid biosynthesis; L-leucine biosynthesis; L-leucine from 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate: step 3/4
Belongs to the isocitrate and isopropylmalate dehydrogenases family
The sequence shown here is derived from an EMBL/GenBank/DDBJ whole genome shotgun (WGS) entry which is preliminary data

citation.title: Sequence and annotation of 42 cannabis genomes reveals extensive copy number variation in cannabinoid synthesis and pathogen resistance genes.

texts.value: Belongs to the LDH2/MDH2 oxidoreductase family

document.claim_boundary: One representative weak broad-name hit, not a characterized Cannabis enzyme. Coordinates replay the original full-proteome screen. Domain overlap and automated annotations do not establish ureidoglycolate catalysis or an alternative exact activity. Original thresholds and failed-screen result are unchanged.

claims.access_scope: Publisher article text: abstract, structural comparison, functional analysis, discussion, and cloning sections; supplementary plots not inspected.
claims.claim: The E. coli AllD study reports NAD preference and a structural explanation involving Asp308/Gln309. The R48A and H116A mutants lacked measured activity. These are reference-enzyme observations, not Cannabis annotations.
claims.boundary: Does not establish reverse flux, a Cannabis homolog, or NADP activity. Residue conservation alone would not establish substrate specificity.

claims.claim: EC 1.1.1.350 separates the NAD-specific activity and lists reviewed reference proteins P58408 and P77555.
EC 1.1.1.154 includes both cofactor equations and describes dual activity in Arthrobacter allantoicus; it does not supply a reviewed sequence in this entry.

claims.access_scope: Indexed publisher abstract excerpt; direct page fetch failed; full paper not reviewed.
claims.claim: The Arthrobacter purification study reports conversion of S-ureidoglycolate to oxalurate using either NAD or NADP.
claims.boundary: No exact assayed-protein sequence has been resolved here. Do not equate a name or EC match with sequence-linked biochemical evidence.

document.decision: Preserve separate cofactor-specific gaps. Do not transfer the E. coli NAD reference assignment to the NADP equation.
next_tests: Resolve the assayed Arthrobacter strain and protein sequence from the original purification study before assigning a dual-cofactor reference.

For any future Cannabis lead, assay chemically verified S-ureidoglycolate and oxalurate with NAD/NADH and NADP/NADPH separately, using substrate-decay and no-protein controls and product identification.
Test both directions independently; an oxidation assay does not establish synthesis in the selected reverse route.

claim_boundary: Lossless reference-gap reviews, generic-substrate searches and experimental hypotheses. Negative searches do not establish enzyme absence. Generic substrate annotations and in-vitro chemical interconversion do not close exact Cannabis reaction gaps. Historical balanced network and atom tracing unchanged.
